subject: Request amplification: customer SDK retry loop causing 5xx/429 surge
messages:
From: Alex Konstant <alex.konstant@packetwise.io>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: maria.gomez@packetwise.io
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 18:12:00 -0400
Subject: Sudden 429/5xx spike after SDK rollout — need help

Hi Sean / Monica,

Quick heads up — we pushed PacketWise client SDK v2.9.1 to production at ~17:40 EDT and immediately saw a large spike in 429 and 5xx errors against Redwood endpoints. Our service is getting timeouts and clients are retrying aggressively which makes it worse.

Attached: packetwise_error_trace.log (sampling of client-side traces) and a dashboard screenshot.

What we've observed: 
- Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to 6.7% within 10 minutes of the deploy
- High request concurrency from identical client IP ranges
- Our own retries are configured in the SDK (max_retries=10, retry_backoff=0 in this release) — that was a bug in the default profile.

Can Redwood tell us if you're seeing a server-side surge? Any short-term mitigation we should do while we roll back the SDK? This is impacting a handful of our larger enterprise customers.

Thanks,
Alex
Principal Engineer, PacketWise

--

Monica / Rishi — forwarding PacketWise's alert. They claim the SDK default landed with aggressive retries (max 10, no jitter). If true, this can create a classic retry amplification loop.

Immediate ask: 
- Monica: can you engage on-call infra (and suggest a temp mitigation we can apply server-side)? Throttling, soft 429 with Retry-After, or temporarily blocking the most active client keys?
- Rishi: can platform put a short-term global token rate limit for this customer until we get their SDK rolled back?

I'll loop in Markus for exec visibility since PacketWise says enterprise customers are impacted.

Thanks — Sean
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 18:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden 429/5xx spike after SDK rollout — need help

Alex — thanks for the quick report and for including the traces. We're seeing the same client-side traffic pattern in our ingress logs: large burst of identical request shapes with very short inter-request intervals. That pattern is consistent with an aggressive retry loop on the client.

Short-term mitigations (we can apply within ~10 minutes):
- Add a temporary per-token soft-rate-limit for PacketWise's production API key (preferentially 50% of current steady-state)
- Enable a server-side jittered 429 response that includes Retry-After for their clients
- Blackhole the top 5 offending IPs if we identify they are test traffic

Longer-term: we recommend they ship an SDK patch that sets an exponential backoff with jitter and reduces max_retries to 3.

Can you confirm you can cut a rollback or ship a fix? If not, we'll apply the soft-rate-limit and visible Retry-After header to reduce amplification.

- Monica
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 00:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sudden 429/5xx spike after SDK rollout — need help

Alex — appreciate the rollback update. PacketWise reported partial improvement after the rollback, but a residual elevated error rate remains during the propagation window. We applied the temporary per-token soft-rate-limit and added Retry-After headers; that reduced peak amplification by ~60%.

We will:
- Schedule a joint postmortem for Mon 09:00 EDT to confirm root cause and remediation steps
- Provide a short SDK guidance doc and a patch recommendation for PacketWise's open-source client to prevent regressions
- Track impact and consider a small one-time credit if downstream customers were materially impacted (will loop in finance)

For transparency, preliminary root cause appears to be: PacketWise SDK defaults changed in v2.9.1 to aggressive immediate retries (max_retries=10, backoff=0) and a bug where 429 responses were not honoring Retry-After, causing immediate replays. Combined with our burst-sensitive routing, this created a transient overload and elevated 5xxs.

We'll capture a full timeline and remediation checklist for the postmortem.

- Monica

Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:42:00 -0400
Subject: Resolution & next steps — PacketWise retry loop incident (INC-20270328)

Alex / Maria — thanks again for the fast collaboration. Quick summary and actions from our side:

Timeline (short):
- 17:40 EDT: PacketWise SDK v2.9.1 rollout begins
- 17:46 EDT: elevated 429/5xx observed in Redwood ingress metrics
- 17:52 EDT: PacketWise notified; rollback started
- 18:00–18:12 EDT: Redwood applied soft-rate-limit and Retry-After header to PacketWise token
- 18:24 EDT: PacketWise rollback propagation mostly complete; error rate decreased ~85%

Preliminary root cause: PacketWise client SDK introduced aggressive immediate retries (max_retries=10, no jitter) and did not respect 429/Retry-After semantics. This produced a retry amplification loop under load that briefly overloaded our routing tier leading to timeouts and elevated 5xxs.

Action items (owners):
- PacketWise: publish fixed SDK v2.9.2 with exponential backoff + jitter and max_retries=3; notify customers to upgrade (Alex)
- Redwood Infra (Rishi): implement optional server-side safeguard that honors 429/Retry-After and caps client-side token concurrency for a single key (short-term feature flag)
- Redwood SDK/Docs (Monica): publish guidance and set our SDK default to jittered exponential backoff (max_retries=3) with clear migration notes
- Finance (Markus): review potential credits for affected enterprise customers and advise on comms

Follow-up: joint postmortem Monday 09:00 EDT (calendar invite sent). We'll produce an incident report and recommended SDK changes by EOD Mon.

If you want a temporary dedicated capacity allocation while PacketWise upgrades, Rishi / Markus are on cc to discuss.

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

--
